name: The Six Kingdoms
description: The kingdoms of the Greater Lands.

name: The Nine States
description: The emirates, sultanates, cities and states of the Greater Lands.

name: The Union of the Kingdoms
description: A former union, broken back into Miurna, Leantis and Godrastan when the court fragmented after the assassination of the Prince of Miurna.

name: Kingdom of Miurna
description: Claims the Lost Prince as its true heir; controlled by a younger son.

name: Kingdom of Leantis
description: Claims the Lost Prince as its true heir; controlled by a younger son.

name: Godrastan
description: Claims the Lost Prince as its true heir; controlled by the court elders. Strict naturalist laws.

name: The Palatinate
description: The True Way is most active here and in the High Marks.

name: The High Marks
description: A collection of Electors and Principalities. Politically astute enough not to challenge the Engineers, though they covet Engineer equipment and techniques.

name: Emirate of Ievure
description: Held by the younger brother of the Sultana of Caryes.

name: Sultanate of Astina
description: Known as the Harem.

name: Sevine & Caryes
description: The Sultana was heir to Caryes; Caryes negotiated a union with the Principality of Sevine, which owed fealty to her, to stop her personal union breaking up on her death.

name: The Rock of Aphemenosta
description: The Sultana was its heir through her mother.

name: The Engineers
description: The unnamed empire (in the projection: the UK and Ireland). Publicly neutral on religion and state; in fact they trade technology for inviolable patents and control of rivers and ports, and suppress learning and magic as threats to their monopoly. Their materially interesting technology destructs if tampered with.

name: The Empire of the Sun
description: In the projection: North and Central America.

name: The Sandfolk
description: In the projection: the US Midwest.

name: The Dragon Seat
description: In the projection: Indonesia.

name: The Threefold Republic
description: In the projection: Sudan, Chad, CAR, Cameroon, Nigeria and Benin.

name: The Elven Islands
description: In the projection: Madagascar and Malaysia.

name: The Tribes of Hanathy
description: In the projection: South America.

name: The Ancients
description: The Gamemasters.

name: The Keepers of Mantra
description: In the projection: Svalbard.

name: The Eastern Emirates
description: Separately, in the projection: Morocco, Mauritania, Senegal, Gambia, Algeria and Tunisia.

name: The Sapphire Kingdom
description: The Sapphire Throne: an autocratic arch-enemy of the Engineers (in the projection: Yemen, Djibouti, Eritrea). Feeds the Order of the White Raven controlled knowledge of magic and technology in return for its operations against the Engineers.

name: The Universal Church
description: Ubiquitous; nominally the church of state in all of the Six Kingdoms and Nine States, broad to the point of dilution. Seen by its critics as a willing tool of the Engineers.

name: The True Way
description: Also called the True Church. A hard-line, reactionary branch of the Church seeking to restore the political and religious authority and dogmatism it once held; excommunicated and considered heretical. Most active in the Palatinate and the High Marks.

name: The Order of the White Raven
description:
A tiny, highly secretive transnational network of faithful pragmatists, mostly of the Universal Church, fewer than 200 across the world, with a handful of supporters among the clergy and regional tribes. Some of the few magic-trained natives of the Greater Lands, through secret tomes.

- They hold the True Church dogmatic and the Universal Church a corrupted tool of the apostate Engineers, and believe the prohibitions on magic and the failure of independent science are Engineer manipulation.
- They seek true independence and self-determination for the Kingdoms and States, but cannot move publicly until times change.
- They search for the child of the Prince of Miurna and the Sultana of Caryes.
- Founded at the Raven of Carrowmore in Linos; messages and donations go through the bakery in Candlesham.

name: The Committee Exterior
description:
The Imperial-Delegate Executive Committee-in-Principal for the Good Administration of Exterior Affairs. Has found the ore-rich dunes and set up an enclave and a rare Artificer's Workshop. Spreads the belief that cooperation with the Engineers is the only route to engineering and science, and quietly promotes folk superstition and vice to keep its monopoly on research and natural knowledge.

*Seeds:* Protectors, Outlander · Resourceful, Collaborative · Wealth · Agenda: spread a belief; obstacle: a key piece of information must first be discovered.

name: The Guilds of the High Marks
description:
Strongly structured and secretive, held together by strict discipline. They covet Engineer technology and hold several secret pieces they cannot dismantle; they seek any they can find, not least for its loan or resale value. In this region, mostly active among the farmers of the Dells.

*Seeds:* Merchants, Farmers · Disciplined, Collaborative · Alliances, Apparatus, Magic · Agenda: collect artifacts; obstacle: it must happen at a rare or exact moment.

name: The True Church Lay Clergy
description:
Lay clergy of the True Church in the farming communities, mostly secret but sometimes locally known. They resent the Engineers' exploitation of the once-sacred black dunes and their treatment of the Western Dells, and want the Engineer stronghold gone, but know open conflict is politically untenable. If the balance holds, they hope to restore the Church as it was, beyond both the Engineers and the vacillating Universal Church.

*Seeds:* Military, Farmer · Resourceful, Deceptive · Lineage, Information, Ruthlessness, Members, Conviction · Agenda: revive a former power; obstacle: a powerful figure or foe must be eliminated.
